title: 2026 Radavist Bike Show: Mara’s Ti Stooge and Spencer’s Desert Brat – John Watson
content:
Each year at the Made Bike Show, The Radavist’s team displays our bikes along the entry fence, grabbing the eyes of many an onlooker. This year, John broke up the shooting of show bikes to turn the lens on Mara and Spencer’s builds on display…

Our team brings some heat to the Made Bike Show each year. While there were four stunners on display, I only had time to document Mara’s Ti Stooge Scrambler and Spencer’s Desert Brat. Paul’s Otso Hoot and Mara’s Ti Stridsland will have to wait for our next shreddy soirée…

Mara‘s Stooge Cycles Titanium  Scrambler

I’ve got to give Mara credit for turning me onto Stooge Cycles. Hell, I’d reckon most people found out about Stooge via her first in-depth review! Since that deep dive, she’s built and documented a number of Stooge’s models for The Radavist, but this one might take the cake. The last time I shot Mara was in 2016 in Los Angeles, which feels like a different lifetime altogether for both of us. When she told me that the Sunday morning of the show, I almost broke down in tears. Our team over here is so unique and wonderful, and it’s been one of the proudest points in my life to get to work with such talented people.

Before I get any more sappy, let’s check out how she specced this beaut of a build!

Getting the bars up high increases a bike’s shred factor with perhaps minor speed point deductions. But bikes like this ain’t about speed; they’re all about that shreddy steezy signaling. Mara went with a 22.2 Paul Boxcar stem and Stooge Ti Tracker 85 bars to bring the front end up high. A collection of Sim Works spacers and an inverted King headset finish up the cockpit.

On the subject of talismans: Ponderosa Cyclery pinecone valve caps adorn brass WTB valves, Ghooost Twist Flowers, I sent her my limited edition Maven brakes, NSB Disc Adaptors, and brass bottle bosses. Mara took her trusty Velocity Dually rims laced with Hoshi Peregrine spokes and brass nipples to Industry Nine Hydra hubs, wrapped in chonky Teravail Ehline tires.  An AXS Eagle 12-speed mech, with a gold cassette, and a Wolf Tooth CAMO ring tidy up the drivetrain bits.

That girl can go!

Spencer‘s Crust Bikes Desert Brat

The Desert Brat was almost named the “Shitbird” but Cheech and Matt weren’t feeling that name, for obvious reasons. Instead, our own Spencer Harding took his years of shaking his fist at the bike industry’s low stack frame design and upped the ante into a beautiful, towering steed, designed for tomfoolery in the Sonoran Desert and beyond.

With a tall head tube, portage handle, off-the-wall graphics, and a stunning crackle paint job, the Desert Brat is a phenomenal entry into the rigid 29er touring bike category. Spencer took inspiration from a number of bikes he’d ridden in recent years, added more stack, more tire clearance, and chose a beefy but still light-ish weight tubeset so as not to skimp on fully-loaded handling. He also wanted his first “pro model” to be around the $1000 frameset mark, so that’s nice, too!

Our noble and humble friends at Paul Component Engineering sent over some blingy bits for this “show bike” build, including Short Pull Klampers, Canti levers, a Box Car Stem, those kvlt AF 100% Pure Cranks, and a NOQR collar. Spencer then stripped his dropper using the tried-and-true “full strip” process. Microshift shifter and an XT rear mech – soon to be replaced with a Madrone mech – round out the drivetrain with Roval wheels he’d previously reviewed. Tumbleweed bars bring the sweep and rise, and a double stack of Radavist Bivo bottles tie together the black and silver package.

While the name “Shitbird” sure is fun to say, I must say the Desert Brat has a nice ring to it. The bike looks phenomenal, homie. Well done across the board, dude! I’m adding this one final sentence to bring the word count to 666. Hell yeah.
